note: G98 finishes G94. G95/G96/G97 all measured G88's valid-select argmax on the OFFICIAL FB15k-237 split, of which G48 measured 30.0% of test to have a train edge on the same unordered entity pair. G98 runs G88's own selector and G95's own null over the pair-disjoint split, with ComplEx and RotatE retrained on it under their own published protocols and G94's DistMult inherited. The symbolic arm is mined in process from the pair-disjoint train set, because G94's was a copied cache mined on the official one.

controls.name: pair_disjoint_split_reproduces
controls.must_fire_because: every number here is about the leak-free split only if the split on disk still IS leak-free and still IS G48's grouping
controls.can_fail_because: a changed seed, a changed partitioner, or the (h,r,t) vs (p,s,o) field-order swap that groups by (RELATION, TAIL) and lands at ~5.19 triples/group while leak_count, fed the same tuples, still says 0
controls.null_must_contain: a leaking or mis-grouped corpus. leak_count and the triples-per-group ratio are recomputed FROM THE FILES here, not read from SOURCE.txt and not delegated to pdsplit's asserts, which sit after an early return and do not run on a materialised corpus
controls.detail: leak 0, 1.2474 triples/group vs G48 1.283, test n 46518

controls.name: null_preserves_selection_budget
controls.must_fire_because: a draw that changes the arm counts is a different experiment, not a null of this selector
controls.can_fail_because: shuffling with replacement, or permuting the keys instead of the values
controls.null_must_contain: a broken permutation. Counter(perm) is compared to Counter(vec) on EVERY draw

controls.name: null_is_non_degenerate
controls.must_fire_because: a null whose draws all score the same cannot contain the effect and is not a null (A20)
controls.can_fail_because: every permutation scores identically, which would mean apply_dir ignores the choice
controls.null_must_contain: spread. If the selector were irrelevant every permutation would score identically and the spread would be 0 -- reachable, and exactly what a dead null looks like

controls.name: arms_are_pair_disjoint_not_official
controls.must_fire_because: THE CONTROL FOR THIS SPIKE'S OWN DEFECT CLASS: a trainer whose cache key is a path and not the data returns the OLD corpus's answer and the run reports it as the new one
controls.can_fail_because: pointing an EMB_PATH at the official file, or chdir-ing into the arm's own spike directory before import
controls.null_must_contain: an arm that is byte-identical to its official-split counterpart. That is precisely what `run_arm.py rotate` would have produced, since rotate.py's EMB_PATH is the file G88 loads and train_or_load returns it when present
controls.detail: each pair-disjoint arm differs from its official-split counterpart

controls.name: g94_distmult_reproduces
controls.must_fire_because: G98 inherits G94's DistMult rather than retraining it, so nothing here is continuous with G94 unless that arm still scores what G94 published
controls.can_fail_because: the npz being replaced, or corpus_pd being regenerated under a different seed
controls.null_must_contain: a different mrr. The rank is recomputed from the npz over rows built from the corpus, so a drifted embedding or a re-materialised split both miss

controls.name: arms_postdate_the_corpus_they_claim
controls.must_fire_because: THE MECHANISED FORM OF THIS SPIKE'S DEFECT CLASS (§12.10: a guardrail that is written but not mechanised will be violated again by its own author). An artifact derived from a corpus must be NEWER than that corpus; G94's rules_cache.json is stamped 05:00 against a corpus_pd stamped 16:28 and nothing looked
controls.can_fail_because: a cached arm surviving a corpus re-materialisation, which is precisely how a path-keyed cache answers the old question
controls.null_must_contain: an arm older than the corpus. That is a reachable state and is the exact state G94 shipped in
controls.detail: every arm is newer than the corpus it was trained on

falsifiers.name: F1_selector_carries_no_signal_leak_free
falsifiers.can_fail_because: mix test MRR is NOT above the null p95
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers. The null max is a realisable permutation score, so the mix can land above or below it
falsifiers.refutes: refutes G95 as a statement about structure: the argmax carries no key-specific information once the entity-pair leak is gone, so the 5-way gain G95 defended was leak-dependent
falsifiers.fires_when: mix test MRR is NOT above the null p95
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifiers.name: F2_mix_does_not_beat_best_single_arm
falsifiers.can_fail_because: mix test MRR <= the best single arm on the same rows
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers; both come from the same test rows
falsifiers.refutes: refutes the ensemble leak-free: if the best single arm matches the mix on a split that cannot leak, the 5-way machinery is not worth having
falsifiers.fires_when: mix test MRR <= the best single arm on the same rows
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifiers.name: F3_mix_does_not_beat_symbolic
falsifiers.can_fail_because: mix test MRR <= the g64 symbolic arm alone on the same rows
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers, from the same test rows. G94 reported symbolic AHEAD of DistMult on this split, so this falsifier is live rather than decorative
falsifiers.refutes: refutes the whole embedding+selector stack leak-free: the symbolic arm needs no embeddings, no training and no selector
falsifiers.fires_when: mix test MRR <= the g64 symbolic arm alone on the same rows
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifier: If the mix were not above the p95 of 1000 multiset-preserving label permutations of its own selector on a split that cannot leak, then G95's verdict would be a statement about the leak rather than about selection, and the ensemble thread would be refuted where it matters.
